text.p: Seamico Securities recommended on Wednesday that investors accumulate Bangkok Bank Plc as the bank is in a better position for recovery due to a strong balance sheet and better asset quality.

Bangkok Bank set aside a loan loss provision of 2.8 billion baht ($112 million) in the fourth quarter alone and, therefore, its entire-year reserves rose 26 percent, Seamico said in its latest report.
The bank's accrued interest dropped from 6.05 billion baht in the third quarter last year to 5.67 billion in the fourth quarter, it said.
"The most interesting management strategy is that of Bangkok Bank. The bank had apparently restructured some of tis non-performing loans in Q4 1996," it said.

"In the meantime, its investment in other securities rose from 40 billion baht reported in September 1996 to 53.3 billion in December. We imagine the bank has transformed some of its non-performing loans into equity holdings," it added.
Seamico forecast that lending growth would continue to slow during first half of 1997 and then begin to recover in the second half.
